newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: SOCCER-CAMEROON NEED WIN TO ENSURE WORLD CUP PLACE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CAMEROON NEED WIN TO ENSURE WORLD CUP PLACE.

text.p: Faced with the likelihood of needing to beat Zimbabwe away to guarantee a place in the World Cup finals, Cameroon have enjoyed their usual chaotic preparation for Sunday's match.

Cameroon top group four with 11 points, two clear of Angola and with a goal difference better by two. But with Angola likely to beat bottom of the group Togo, the Indomitable Lions cannot afford to rely on anyone but themselves and must go for the win.
But yet another change of coach, the sending of a virtual reserve team to a warm-up tournament and the now-traditional bonus discussions have hampered their build-up to the game in Harare.

The Lions have never before had to play an away game to clinch World Cup qualification and their record in Harare is poor, having been well beaten 4-1 on their last visit in an African Nations qualifier in January 1995, and losing 1-0 in a 1993 qualifier.
Zimbabwe are out of the running but have a score or two to settle, having been denied a place in both the 1994 World Cup and the 1996 African Nations Cup by Cameroon.
But new coach Jean Manga Onguene, who took over a month ago after the resignation of Henri Depireux, sees a silver lining in the situation.
"I'm not worried about playing away from home," he said. "At home we would have been subjected to a terrible amount of public pressure."
Experienced striker Francois Omam Biyick agreed. "It will be necessary to be strong in order to win away from home," he said.
Cameroon last week limbered up for Harare by taking part in a four nation tournament with Tunisia, Zambia and Nigeria.
They took what amounted to a shadow squad and lost to Nigeria 1-0 before winning the third-place play-off against Zambia 4-3 on penalties following a 3-3 extra-time draw.
"I would have liked to have had my ideal team together in order to be better prepared for Harare. Unfortunately not all the team was here," lamented Onguene.
But he has been spoilt for choice in his Harare line-up, with Jean Jaques Misse-Misse, Alphonse Tchami and Marc Vivien Foe joining Biyick to form an embarrassingly rich collection of forwards.
Mboma, Suffo and Billong are also at hand to provide much-needed experience.

But the team's preparation has been disrupted by the usual squabbling behind the scenes. Belgian coach Depireux resigned at the beginning of July after 10 months in charge, citing differences with his then-assistant Onguene and a lack of Federation co-operation.
Despite his successes in restoring a tattered Cameroonian reputation after a disappointing 1994 World Cup and Nations Cup in South Africa, he was heavily criticised by the local press.
Goalkeeper Jacqes Songo'o made light of the latest shuffle. "The changes at the top aren't very important, although it's a pity Depireux has quit when the team is going well," he said.
Onguene has acted early to try to prevent a recurrence of the wrangles over bonuses that have previously caused so many internal problems.
"The bonuses for qualification will be announced before the game to avoid those last minute problems," he said.
All they need to do now is qualify.
